proof.text: Prove a general closed-subset induction criterion for a sheaf F on a Noetherian scheme S. For every closed immersion i:Z to S with nonempty Z, assume a nonempty open U of Z where i inverse F is constructible. Induct on the image closed subset of i using WellFoundedLT.induction. The image of the closed complement of U is strictly smaller because i is injective and U has a point. Glue the two restrictions using the proved open-closed criterion for constructible sheaves. Empty schemes have the empty stratification. Taking i to be the identity proves the criterion. It allows arbitrary nilpotent structures on closed bases, so no reduction of S is needed.

Fix the original degree and use the criterion. The base is Noetherian by finite type over Z. Every closed subscheme is Noetherian and affine. Base-changing h to it preserves smooth relative dimension one, affineness and separatedness. The compact-support base-change natural isomorphism, exact inverse image and the constant-pullback isomorphism identify the restricted cohomology with compact support of the finite constant module on this new curve. The comparison between the two constructibility predicates lets us work with the existing finite-stalk API.

Over a nonempty Noetherian affine base choose a generic point of an irreducible component and apply the good-curves generic diagram. The chosen generic fibre has dimension at most one by the smooth relative dimension bound. An open of a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact; the finite cover V of U is therefore Noetherian and qcqs. Compact-support base change and constant pullback identify pullback of the original cohomology to V. Surjective-pullback descent reduces constructibility on U to constructibility over V.

The closed complement Z of W in the curve over V is quasi-finite. On each fibre embed it as the complement of the given dense open. In a Noetherian sober space of dimension at most one, this complement has dimension at most zero: the generic point of each irreducible component is in the dense open, so adjoining it strictly extends every specialization chain in the complement. The finite-type fibre is then locally Artinian and discrete. This proves the required open-singleton fibre condition. The constant module in degree zero has constructible cohomology by its single finite locally constant stratum. Apply quasi-finite shriek constructibility to Z.

For each proper smooth model p_i, use the identity compactification: identity extension by zero is the identity, so its compact-support functor is its derived direct image. Apply the proper-smooth-curves finite-module theorem. The finite etale map t_i is quasi-finite, so its shriek sends this complex to one with constructible cohomology. The qcqs composition isomorphism identifies it with compact support for p_i followed by t_i, for every prescribed compactification. These are exactly the model hypotheses of the new good-curves-preimage lemma.

Apply the good-curves-preimage constructibility lemma using the models from the previous step. This gives constructibility on P=nu inverse W. The map P to W is a closed immersion surjective on points by the diagram. Its complementary open is empty. Apply the open-closed compact-support triangle with this closed immersion. The first object is zero: sheaves on the empty scheme are zero and the additive single, inverse-image, compact-support and inclusion functors preserve zero objects. The Serre homology property of the distinguished triangle therefore transfers constructibility from P to W.

The open-closed compact-support triangle for W in the curve has constructible outer cohomology by the preceding steps. The constructible homology property is triangulated because constructible sheaves form a weak Serre class, so the middle object has constructible cohomology. This proves the generic step over V; descent proves it on the nonempty U. The closed-subset criterion from step 1 completes the original claim, and the comparison with finite-constant-value constructibility gives exactly the unchanged statement.

The compactified dense-open calculation is isolated as lem-weil-pbc-good-curves-preimage-constructible.

title: Constant finite coefficients on affine smooth relative curves
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Work in the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For any separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$ consists of a quasi-compact open immersion $j$ and a proper morphism $p$ with $h=pj$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]; write $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A$ is a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra. Let $h:X\to S$ be a separated affine smooth morphism of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; let $M$ be a finite $\Lambda$-module and $\underline M$ the constant sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-constructible-locally-constant], placed in degree zero. Then $\mathcal H^q(Rh_!^c\underline M)$ is constructible for every integer $q$ and every compactification $c$ of $h$.
